title: DPA: Clarify training carve-out language, subprocessors & e- signature
text:
DPA: Clarify training carve-out language, subprocessors & e- signature

['From: Amira Hassan <amira.hassan@zephrhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Daniel Park <d.park@zephrhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines: training exclusion + subprocessor list

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft. Our legal team reviewed and attached redlines (Zephr_DPA_redlines_20260525.pdf). Two priority items for us:

1) Training / Model Improvement carve-out — current language refers broadly to "model improvements". We need an explicit exclusion that Customer Content (defined as PII and PHI contained in data we provide) will not be used to train or improve models, nor to derive model weights or derivative models, unless there is an explicit opt-in amendment.

2) Subprocessors & transfers — please provide the current subprocessor list and confirm the transfer mechanism for EU data (SCCs or adequacy). Also need a 30-day notice for onboarding new subprocessors and the right to object.

We'd like to resolve these redlines by close of week. Attaching the redline PDF for reference.

Thanks,

Amira Hassan
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Zephr Health
amira.hassan@zephrhealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Zephr_DPA_redlines_20260525.pdf', 'From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Amira Hassan <amira.hassan@zephrhealth.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <d.park@zephrhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: training exclusion + subprocessor list

Amira — thanks for the clear notes and the PDF. Looping in Neha (privacy) and Laura (security) to review the carve-out language and transfer mechanics.

High level — we can offer one of two approaches to satisfy Zephr's ask:

Option A (preferred, minimal disruption): Add a narrowly scoped addendum that defines "Customer Confidential Data" and states that such data will not be used for model training, model updates, or derivative model creation. This preserves our ability to use aggregated, non-identifiable system telemetry for service improvements.

Option B (stricter): Flat prohibition on using any Customer Content for any model training or fine-tuning, with audit rights and an extended subprocessors notice period. This is feasible but will change operational defaults and affect cost.

I've attached a proposed addendum (RDW_Proposed_Addendum_20260530.docx) that implements Option A with a strong definition and a 30-day subprocessor notice + objection window. If Zephr accepts, we can route this via DocuSign and include the finalized subprocessor list as an exhibit.

Proposed next steps: please confirm which option you prefer by EOD Wednesday and we'll prepare a DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
+1 (650) 555-0122

Attachments: RDW_Proposed_Addendum_20260530.docx', 'From: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 11:19:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA redlines: training exclusion + subprocessor list

Jonas / Laura — quick privacy/security take. I've edited the addendum language below; if we go Option A this is what I recommend including verbatim in the addendum body (keeps the carve-out tight and auditable):

"Definition: \"Customer Confidential Data\" means Customer Content that contains Personal Data, Protected Health Information, or other data designated as confidential by Customer in writing that is provided to Redwood Inference under the Master Agreement.

Training Exclusion: Redwood shall not use Customer Confidential Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve the weights or parameters of any foundation model, nor shall Redwood create derivative or standalone models using Customer Confidential Data, except where Customer provides a separate written opt-in amendment.

Service Improvements: Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified usage metrics (not reverse-engineerably tied to Customer or Individuals) generated from its systems for service operation, monitoring, and non-model research improvements.

Subprocessors / Transfers: Provide current subprocessor list as Exhibit A; 30 days prior notice for new subprocessors; Customer may object in writing within 30 days. For transfers from EU to US, parties will rely on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or an alternative lawful transfer mechanism agreed in writing."

Also recommend a short audit clause (on-site or remote) limited to the training exclusion — audit frequency once per 12 months and subject to mutual NDA.

If that sounds acceptable I'll prep tracked-changes for the addendum and the subprocessor exhibit.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

', 'From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Amira Hassan <amira.hassan@zephrhealth.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <d.park@zephrhealth.com>, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed DPA addendum (tracked) + DocuSign link

Amira — thanks again for the redlines. We've incorporated Neha's language into an addendum and attached the tracked-changes version. Key points in the attached RDW_Proposed_Addendum_20260530.docx:

- Clear definition of "Customer Confidential Data" and an explicit prohibition on using that data for model training or deriving model weights without an explicit, separate opt-in.
- Allowance for aggregated and de-identified usage metrics for monitoring and product improvements (not model weight updates).
- Subprocessor exhibit attached; 30-day notice + objection right.
- EU transfers: we will adhere to SCCs; will provide executed SCCs as an exhibit for EU customers.

If the addendum is acceptable, I've prepared a DocuSign envelope for the addendum + exhibit so we can sign and complete this quickly. Link: https://app.docusign.com/Envelopes/details/6789 (DocuSign envelope ready).

Would you prefer we:
- (A) Sign the addendum now and continue operational alignment on subprocessors, or
- (B) Sign only after Zephr confirms the subprocessor exhibit?

If you give the green light on (A) we'll send for signature today and attach the executed copy to the HubSpot deal.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: RDW_Proposed_Addendum_20260530.docx; Subprocessor_Exhibit_May2026.xlsx

Subject: Re: Proposed DPA addendum (tracked) + DocuSign link

Jonas — appreciate the quick turnaround. The proposed wording in the addendum looks good and consistent with what Zephr needs. One quick question before I countersign: when you say "aggregated, de-identified usage metrics" — can those include derived performance metrics (latency/error rates) that help you tune routing and autoscaling but not influence model weights? We're OK with those for service ops, but want to be sure there's a clear line that such metrics won't be fed back to training pipelines.

I've signed the envelope in DocuSign (Envelope ID: 6789) and attached the executed PDF. Happy to keep the subprocessor exhibit as an ongoing dialogue provided we get 30 days notice and the SCC confirmation for EU data.

Thanks,
Amira Hassan
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Zephr Health
